title: AI Lifestyle Product Photos | AIVideosUGC
description: Create AI lifestyle product photos from one plain image. Place the item in a room, table or cafe scene so shoppers picture using it without a shoot.
h1: AI lifestyle product photos that bring a catalog to life
lead: Place one plain product photo in a room, in a hand, or on a table. Shoppers can picture using it, and you do not need to book a shoot. Credits are what you spend on each scene, and you see that cost before you start.

steps_h2: How to Put Your Product in a Scene
steps_lead: Upload the product, name the place, and download a square scene.

steps.d: Use one photo that shows the whole item. Shape and small details should be easy to see.
Try a room, a table, or a market. Name the surface and one object, so the scene shows how the product is used.
Check the scene against your plain photo, then download the square image for the store or an ad.

faq.q: What are AI lifestyle product photos?
faq.a: They place your real product photo in a room, on a table, or in another everyday setting. You check the result before you publish.

faq.q: How do I make a lifestyle product photo?
faq.a: Upload one product photo, choose or describe the setting, and download a square image. The credit cost appears before you start.

faq.q: Can I use the scene on a product page?
faq.a: Yes. Pair it with a plain product photo when shoppers also need an exact view of the item. Downloads have no watermark, so no logo is stamped on the file. You can use them for your business.
Yes. Pick a room, a cafe, or a market moment, or describe the surface and light you want.

faq.q: Can I change the scene after the first result?
faq.a: Yes. Start again with a different surface or object. Each photo costs 24 credits.

faq.q: Does the scene replace my plain product image?
faq.a: No. Keep the original photo for details. Use the scene when you want shoppers to picture where the item belongs.

faq.q: Can I post the scene in a social ad?
faq.a: Yes. Finish the headline and the offer in your ad editor. The photo does not include your price.

faq.q: How is this different from a photoshoot?
faq.a: A shoot needs a place, a few extra objects, and a day on the calendar. Here you start from a photo you already have. Read [how to take product photos for AI](page:guide-product-photo-tips) if the photo you upload is hard to read.

faq.q: Can I use the scene on a Shopify store?
faq.a: Yes. Download the square image and upload it on the product page yourself. Each photo is 24 credits, shown before you start.

faq.q: Can I post the scene on Instagram?
faq.a: Yes. These square images work as Instagram product scene photos. Add the caption in Instagram, and add any price in your own editor.

faq.q: Can I add text, a logo, or run many photos?
faq.a: Yes. Add a short line of text or your logo on the scene, or edit a set of photos together. You can also link your store software, called an API, so the store can request new scenes. Each photo is 24 credits, shown before you start. There is no free plan.

platforms.h2: Your Full Set of Product Image Tools
platforms.lead: Create and edit product photos for the store, a marketplace, and ads. Start from one picture or your whole product list.

items.d: Take the old background off and put a clean studio setting behind the item.
Describe a color or a surface. The product should still look like the photo you uploaded.
Put the item on a table, on a shelf, or in a hand so shoppers see daily use. That is the scene this page makes.
Brighten the photo, remove an extra object, and size it for a store page or an ad.
Place clothing or an accessory on a generated person so shoppers can judge the fit.
Download a square photo with no watermark, so no logo is stamped on it. Use it on the site, a marketplace, or an ad. You add the price yourself.
Make the light, detail, and color more even on the photo you already have, before the scene goes up.
Turn a tall photo into a wide one, or the other way, when a store or app wants a different shape.
Link your store software, called an API, so it can ask for a new scene from your product list. Each photo still costs 24 credits, shown before you start.
Place a short offer or the product name on the finished scene. The price still comes from you, not from the photo.
Apply one background or one size to a set of photos together, instead of opening them one by one.
Hand a scene to a teammate for a look before it goes on the product page.
Save the logo, the fonts, and the colors you reuse, so the next scene still looks like your shop.
Make a simple logo when the shop does not have one yet, then place it on later photos.
Open the same photos from a phone or a computer and keep going.
